'''Diane Margaret Maclagan''' (born 1974)<ref>Birth year from [http://id.loc.gov/authorities/names/n2012050395.html Library of Congress catalog entry], retrieved 2019-03-03.</ref> is a professor of [[mathematics]] at the [[University of Warwick]].<ref name=profile>{{citation|url=https://warwick.ac.uk/fac/sci/maths/people/staff/diane_maclagan/|title=Dr Diane Maclagan|publisher=Warwick Mathematics Institute|accessdate=2019-06-03}}</ref> She is a researcher in combinatorial and computational [[commutative algebra]] and [[algebraic geometry]], with an emphasis on [[toric variety|toric varieties]], [[Hilbert scheme]]s, and [[tropical geometry]].

== Education and career ==
As a student at [[Burnside High School]] in [[Christchurch]], New Zealand, Maclagan competed in the [[International Mathematical Olympiad]] in 1990 and 1991, earning a bronze medal in 1991.<ref>{{cite journal|page=10|department=Notices|title=The 32nd International Mathematical Olympiad|first=G. A.|last=Hookings|journal=Newsletter of the New Zealand Mathematical Society|volume=53|date=December 1991|url=http://nzmathsoc.org.nz/downloads/newsletters/NZMSnews53_Dec1991.pdf}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.imo-official.org/participant_r.aspx?id=2559|title=Diane Maclagan - International Mathematical Olympiad|website=www.imo-official.org|access-date=2019-03-30}}</ref> As an undergraduate, she studied at the [[University of Canterbury]], graduating in 1995.<ref name=cv2010>{{citation|url=https://homepages.warwick.ac.uk/staff/D.Maclagan/MaclaganCV2010.pdf|title=Curriculum vitae|year=2010|accessdate=2018-09-30}}</ref> She did her PhD at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], graduating in 2000. Her dissertation, ''Structures on Sets of Monomial Ideals'', was supervised by [[Bernd Sturmfels]].<ref name=cv2010/><ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=44193}}</ref>

After postdoctoral research at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]], Maclagan was a Szegő Assistant Professor at [[Stanford University]] from 2001 to 2004, an assistant professor at [[Rutgers University]] from 2004 to 2007, then an associate professor there from 2007 to 2009. She moved to her present position at the [[University of Warwick]] in 2007.<ref name=cv2010/>

==Books==
